UnsupportedTemporality is returned by the Prometheus connector when the
snapshot is not cumulative — a delta one, which the exposition format
cannot express, or a hand-built one whose temporality is unresolved.

non-monotonic sum Meter cannot.

symbols.name: CanonicalName
symbols.doc: CanonicalName spells a function the same way whoever named it.

symbols.name: CaptureCPU

(503); errors.Is still finds the context's error.

symbols.name: CaptureFailed

profile.

symbols.name: CaptureHeap

CodeCaptureCanceled identifies a CPU capture whose context ended before its
window (0.3.89.3).

CodeCaptureFailed identifies a profile runtime/pprof could not write
(0.3.89.4).

stacks exceed MaxFrames (0.3.89.6).

CodeWindowInvalid identifies a CPU window not positive or over MaxCPUWindow
(0.3.89.1).

DefaultFlameMaxDepth is how deep the flame graph goes when
FoldConfig.FlameMaxDepth is not positive.

symbols.doc:
DefaultFlameMinShare prunes a flame frame costing less than this share of
the total when FoldConfig.FlameMinShare is outside (0, 1): half a percent.

FoldConfig.TopFunctions is not positive.

DefaultTopPerOwner is how many functions each owner's Top lists when
FoldConfig.TopPerOwner is not positive.

symbols.name: FlameRoot
symbols.doc: FlameRoot is the name of a flame graph's root frame.

symbols.name: Fold
symbols.doc: Fold charges every sample of p to an owner and adds it all up.

symbols.name: FoldConfig
symbols.doc: FoldConfig says how Fold reads a profile; every zero field has a default.

symbols.name: Folded
symbols.doc: Folded is a profile folded, in the sample type's own unit.

symbols.name: Frame
symbols.doc: Frame is one frame of a stack.

symbols.name: FunctionCost
symbols.doc: FunctionCost is what one function cost.

symbols.name: Goroutine
symbols.doc: Goroutine is one goroutine, as the runtime's dump describes it.

symbols.name: GoroutineGroup
symbols.doc: GoroutineGroup is goroutines sharing their labels, state and top frame.

symbols.name: Goroutines
symbols.doc: Goroutines returns every goroutine of the process.

symbols.name: GroupConfig
symbols.doc: GroupConfig says how GroupGoroutines groups.

symbols.name: GroupGoroutines
symbols.doc:
GroupGoroutines groups goroutines by labels, state and top frame, largest
first.

symbols.name: MaxCPUWindow
symbols.doc: MaxCPUWindow is the longest window CaptureCPU samples.

symbols.name: MaxFrames
symbols.doc:
MaxFrames bounds the frames Parse builds: each location's once, and every
copy a sample's stack makes of them.

symbols.name: MaxProfileBytes
symbols.doc: MaxProfileBytes bounds what Parse reads, compressed and inflated alike.

symbols.name: OwnerCost
symbols.doc: OwnerCost is what one owner cost.

symbols.name: Parse
symbols.doc: Parse decodes a pprof profile, gzipped or not.

symbols.name: ParseGoroutines
symbols.doc: ParseGoroutines reads a goroutine dump; it never fails.

symbols.name: Profile
symbols.doc: Profile is a decoded pprof profile.

symbols.name: ProfileMalformed

code.public: That is not a well-formed pprof profile

symbols.doc:
ProfileMalformed refuses bytes that are not a well-formed pprof profile —
the field names the part, the input is never quoted — and a nil profile or
a sample short of values handed to Fold.

symbols.name: ProfileTooLarge

code.public: The profile is too large to read

symbols.doc:
ProfileTooLarge refuses a profile over MaxProfileBytes, compressed or
inflated, or whose stacks would take more than MaxFrames frames.

symbols.name: ProfilerBusy

code.public: A CPU profile is already being recorded

symbols.doc:
ProfilerBusy refuses a CPU capture while the process's one CPU profiler is
running, whoever started it (409).

symbols.name: Sample
symbols.doc: Sample is one sample: a stack, a value per sample type, and labels.

symbols.name: SampleType
symbols.doc: SampleType names what a value measures and its unit.

symbols.name: SampleTypeMissing

code.public: The profile does not measure that

symbols.doc:
SampleTypeMissing refuses a fold asked for a sample type the profile does
not measure.

symbols.name: WindowInvalid

code.public: A CPU profile needs a window longer than zero and at most five minutes

symbols.doc: WindowInvalid refuses a CPU window not positive or over MaxCPUWindow (400).

symbols.name: AlwaysSample
symbols.doc: AlwaysSample keeps every root trace.

symbols.name: Attr
symbols.doc:
Attr is one typed dimension. It is the SAME type as
[github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/observe/metrics.Attr], deliberately: an attribute is
OTel's common.proto, shared by every signal, so a value built for a metric is
accepted by a span and the reverse.

symbols.name: AttrKind
symbols.doc: AttrKind discriminates an Attr's value type.

symbols.name: AttrKindBool
symbols.doc: AttrKindBool marks a bool-valued attribute.

symbols.name: AttrKindFloat64
symbols.doc: AttrKindFloat64 marks an IEEE-754 double attribute.

symbols.name: AttrKindInt64
symbols.doc: AttrKindInt64 marks a signed 64-bit integer attribute.

symbols.name: AttrKindInvalid
symbols.doc: AttrKindInvalid is the zero value and names no type.

symbols.name: AttrKindString
symbols.doc: AttrKindString marks a string-valued attribute.

symbols.name: AvailableExporters
symbols.doc:
AvailableExporters returns the sorted list of registered names. The OTLP/HTTP
emitter never appears in it.

symbols.name: Bool
symbols.doc: Bool returns a bool-valued attribute.

symbols.name: Carrier
symbols.doc:
Carrier is the two-method surface a header set presents for propagation. It is
exactly http.Header's Get/Set pair, so http.Header satisfies it with no
adapter.

symbols.name: ClientMiddleware
symbols.doc:
ClientMiddleware returns a middleware tracing every outbound request and
INJECTING the traceparent into it. It decorates the RoundTripper, so no call
site can skip it, and it clones the request rather than mutating one the caller
still holds.

symbols.name: ContextWithSpanContext
symbols.doc:
ContextWithSpanContext returns a copy of parent carrying spanContext. An
invalid context is still stored: it is how "this scope deliberately has no
trace" is expressed, and it shadows any outer one.

symbols.name: DefaultMaxSpans
symbols.doc:
DefaultMaxSpans is a Recorder's default bound. There is no "unbounded"
setting, because a buffer nobody drains is how a tracing integration takes a
process down.

symbols.name: DefaultOTLPMaxResponseBytes
symbols.doc: DefaultOTLPMaxResponseBytes caps the response body read: 1 MiB.

symbols.name: DefaultOTLPTimeout
symbols.doc:
DefaultOTLPTimeout bounds one export round trip: 10s, the OpenTelemetry
specification's own default for OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TIMEOUT.

symbols.name: DefaultScopeName
symbols.doc:
DefaultScopeName names this package as the instrumenting library when a caller
declares no scope. It is deliberately NOT the metrics one: a scope names the
library that produced THIS signal.

symbols.name: DuplicateRegistration

code.public: A trace exporter is already registered under that name

symbols.doc: DuplicateRegistration is the boot-time registry panic sentinel.

symbols.name: EncodeOTLPJSON
symbols.doc:
EncodeOTLPJSON renders spans as ONE OTLP/JSON ExportTraceServiceRequest —
exactly the bytes that go in the body of a POST to /v1/traces. It does no I/O,
so an encoding question never becomes a network question.

symbols.name: EntropyFailed

code.public: Trace identifier generation failed to read secure random bytes

symbols.doc:
EntropyFailed is kept for code that matches it: nothing returns it since
Go 1.24, whose crypto/rand.Read never fails, so minting an identifier
cannot fail.

symbols.name: Event
symbols.doc: Event is a timestamped point inside a span.

symbols.name: ExceptionEventName
symbols.doc: ExceptionEventName is the reserved event name RecordError writes.

symbols.name: ExceptionMessageKey
symbols.doc: ExceptionMessageKey names a recorded error's message.

symbols.name: ExceptionTypeKey
symbols.doc: ExceptionTypeKey names a recorded error's stable identity.

symbols.name: Export
symbols.doc: Export ships spans through the SpanExporter registered as name.

symbols.name: ExportFailed

code.public: The trace exporter failed to ship the spans

symbols.doc: ExportFailed wraps an exporter's failure.

symbols.name: ExporterName
symbols.doc: ExporterName is the typed key a SpanExporter registers under.

symbols.name: Extract
symbols.doc:
Extract reads a span context out of carrier, returning the invalid zero value
when there is nothing usable. It returns no error on purpose — see the package
documentation.

symbols.name: FlagSampled
symbols.doc:
FlagSampled is the traceparent sampled bit — the one flag version 00 defines,
and the one the whole sampling design travels in.

symbols.name: Float64
symbols.doc: Float64 returns a double attribute.

symbols.name: FormatTraceParent
symbols.doc:
FormatTraceParent renders a span context as a version-00 traceparent,
reporting ok=false when the context names no joinable span — an all-zero
identifier is a header every conforming receiver must ignore, so there is
nothing to write. Undefined flag bits are masked here, which is where this SDK
acts as a producer.

symbols.name: HTTPRequestMethodKey
symbols.doc: HTTPRequestMethodKey is the request method attribute the middlewares record.

symbols.name: HTTPResponseStatusCodeKey
symbols.doc: HTTPResponseStatusCodeKey is the response status attribute.

symbols.name: Inject
symbols.doc:
Inject writes context into carrier as a traceparent, plus a tracestate when the
vendor list is non-empty. An invalid context writes NOTHING — not an empty
header, not a zero-filled one.

symbols.name: Int64
symbols.doc: Int64 returns a signed-integer attribute.

symbols.name: InvalidAttribute

code.public: An attribute key is empty or repeated, or its value was never set

symbols.doc:
InvalidAttribute is the panic sentinel for an unusable attribute set —
an empty or repeated key, or a value no constructor set — on a span, an
event, a link or a Resource. It is this package's own code; the metrics
one is a different sentinel for the same defect in that signal.

symbols.name: InvalidSampleRatio

code.public: A sampling ratio must be greater than 0 and at most 1

symbols.doc:
InvalidSampleRatio reports a fraction Ratio will not accept — including
exactly 0, which also spells "unconfigured".

symbols.name: InvalidSpanName

code.public: A span name must not be empty

symbols.doc: InvalidSpanName is the panic sentinel for a Start with no name.

symbols.name: InvalidTraceParent

code.public: The traceparent header is not a valid W3C trace context

symbols.doc: InvalidTraceParent reports a traceparent header that cannot be read.

symbols.name: InvalidTraceState

code.public: The tracestate header is not a valid W3C trace state list

symbols.doc: InvalidTraceState reports a tracestate header that cannot be read.

symbols.name: Kind
symbols.doc: Kind says how a span relates to its neighbours.

symbols.name: KindClient
symbols.doc: KindClient is making an outbound synchronous request.

symbols.name: KindConsumer
symbols.doc: KindConsumer is handling a message enqueued earlier.

symbols.name: KindInternal
symbols.doc: KindInternal is work inside one process.

symbols.name: KindProducer
symbols.doc: KindProducer is enqueuing a message handled later, elsewhere.

symbols.name: KindServer
symbols.doc: KindServer is handling an inbound synchronous request.

symbols.name: KindUnspecified
symbols.doc: KindUnspecified is SPAN_KIND_UNSPECIFIED; it resolves to KindInternal.

symbols.name: Link
symbols.doc: Link points at a causally related span in another trace.

symbols.name: LookupExporter
symbols.doc: LookupExporter returns the SpanExporter registered under name.

symbols.name: MaxTraceStateMembers
symbols.doc:
MaxTraceStateMembers is the W3C list cap: 32 members, from the grammar itself
rather than from a ceiling this SDK invented.

symbols.name: NeverSample
symbols.doc:
NeverSample drops every root trace. It exists so "off" has a NAME a reviewer
can grep for, rather than a rate of zero that is indistinguishable from a field
nobody set.

symbols.name: NewOTLPHTTPExporter
symbols.spelled: func(name ExporterName, cfg OTLPHTTPConfig) (exporter SpanExporter, err error)
symbols.doc:
NewOTLPHTTPExporter builds a SpanExporter that POSTs each batch to an OTLP
collector. It is deliberately NOT in the registry: arming a network client from
an import is worse than arming a writer, and no endpoint could be a correct
default. It does not retry either — use OTLPRetryable with
[github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/resilience].

symbols.name: NewOTLPJSONExporter
symbols.doc:
NewOTLPJSONExporter returns a SpanExporter writing each batch to dst as one
newline-terminated OTLP/JSON document. It is not registered — bind it yourself.

symbols.name: NewRecorder
symbols.doc:
NewRecorder builds the in-memory span destination. Its Sink is what a
TracerConfig takes, and its Collect DRAINS — a Recorder has exactly one reader.

symbols.name: NewSpanID
symbols.doc: NewSpanID draws a fresh random span identifier.

symbols.name: NewTraceID
symbols.doc: NewTraceID draws a fresh random trace identifier.

symbols.name: NewTracer
symbols.doc:
NewTracer builds a Tracer from cfg, applying every clamp once. It cannot fail:
every field of TracerConfig has a resolved meaning, and the inputs that CAN be
refused — a sampling ratio, an OTLP endpoint — are refused by their own
constructors before they reach here.

It returns the concrete [SDKTracer] rather than the [Tracer] port, so a caller
keeps Resource and Scope, and anything the concrete type grows later, without
the port having to grow (ADR 0039).

symbols.name: OTLPEndpointInvalid

code.public: The OTLP endpoint must be an absolute http(s) URL with a path

symbols.doc: OTLPEndpointInvalid reports an endpoint that cannot address a collector.

symbols.name: OTLPExportRejected

code.public: The trace collector rejected the export

symbols.doc: OTLPExportRejected reports a permanent refusal by the collector.

symbols.name: OTLPExportUnavailable

code.public: The trace collector is unavailable

symbols.doc: OTLPExportUnavailable reports a transient failure worth retrying.

symbols.name: OTLPHTTPConfig
symbols.doc: OTLPHTTPConfig configures the OTLP/HTTP exporter.

symbols.name: OTLPInvalidSpanContext

code.public: A span carries an all-zero trace or span identifier

symbols.doc: OTLPInvalidSpanContext reports a span with an all-zero identifier.

symbols.name: OTLPPartialSuccess

code.public: The trace collector accepted the request but rejected some spans

symbols.doc: OTLPPartialSuccess reports an accepted request with rejected spans.

symbols.name: OTLPRetryable
symbols.doc:
OTLPRetryable reports whether err is an OTLP/HTTP failure the specification
says may be replayed. Its signature is exactly resilience.RetryConfig.Retryable's.

symbols.name: OTLPSpanNotEnded

code.public: A span reached the exporter without an end time

symbols.doc: OTLPSpanNotEnded reports a span that reached the encoder unended.

symbols.name: OTLPTracesPath
symbols.doc:
OTLPTracesPath is the OTLP/HTTP path for the trace signal. Append it to a
collector's base URL yourself, so the whole address is one readable string.

symbols.name: ParentBased
symbols.doc:
ParentBased returns a Sampler that honours a valid parent's decision and
consults root only at the start of a trace. It is what almost every deployment
wants — see the package documentation on why re-deciding produces a trace with
holes in it. A nil root clamps to AlwaysSample.

symbols.name: ParseSpanID
symbols.doc: ParseSpanID reads 16 lowercase hex digits, refusing an all-zero result.

symbols.name: ParseTraceID
symbols.doc: ParseTraceID reads 32 lowercase hex digits, refusing an all-zero result.

symbols.name: ParseTraceParent
symbols.doc:
ParseTraceParent reads a traceparent header value, with a typed error. It is
the diagnostic form of Extract: use it when you are debugging a header, not
when you are serving a request.

symbols.name: ParseTraceState
symbols.doc:
ParseTraceState reads a tracestate header value. It refuses the whole header
rather than salvaging the members it understood: a half-parsed list forwarded
to the next hop is a list this process invented.

symbols.name: Ratio
symbols.doc:
Ratio returns a Sampler keeping a deterministic fraction of root traces,
decided on the trace id so two services reach the same verdict for the same id.

It REFUSES exactly 0, and that refusal is the point. A float64 left unset, a
JSON document missing the key and a YAML `rate:` with nothing after it all
produce 0.0 — so a rate of zero means both "sample nothing" and "nobody
configured this", and nothing in the type can tell them apart. The failure is
silent: no error, no log, and no telemetry, where the absence of telemetry IS
the symptom. Say NeverSample for none and AlwaysSample (or Ratio(1)) for all.

symbols.name: RecordError
symbols.doc:
RecordError records err on span as the conventional `exception` event and marks
the span ERROR.

It is a helper rather than a Span method because what an error's type is, and
whether recording one should also set the status, are judgements about the
caller's error model — and a port method would freeze this SDK's answer into
every downstream implementation (ADR 0039).

symbols.name: Recorder
symbols.doc:
Recorder accumulates finished spans in memory and hands them out in
batches. It is the in-tree SpanSink.

symbols.name: RecorderConfig
symbols.doc: RecorderConfig configures a Recorder.

symbols.name: RegisterExporter
symbols.doc:
RegisterExporter inserts e under e.Name(). It panics on a nil exporter or a
distinct exporter claiming a taken name.

symbols.name: Resource
symbols.doc:
Resource identifies the producer of the telemetry. The same type a MeterConfig
takes, so a process cannot carry two Resources that disagree about
service.name — which is the key a backend correlates a trace with a metric on.

symbols.name: SDKTracer
symbols.doc:
SDKTracer is the concrete [Tracer] that [NewTracer] returns: the port's
Start, plus Resource and Scope, which read back what it stamps on every
span it starts. The port keeps the name Tracer; this is the SDK's
implementation of it, in OpenTelemetry's sense of API and SDK. Name it
to keep a tracer in a field, or to pass one to a function of your own.

symbols.name: Sampler
symbols.doc:
Sampler decides whether a ROOT trace is recorded. A func port, so it cannot
grow a method at all.

symbols.name: SamplingParams
symbols.doc: SamplingParams is everything a Sampler sees.

symbols.name: Scope
symbols.doc: Scope identifies the instrumentation that started the spans.

symbols.name: ServerAddressKey
symbols.doc: ServerAddressKey is the host attribute.

symbols.name: ServerMiddleware
symbols.doc:
ServerMiddleware returns a middleware tracing every inbound request: it
extracts the parent context from the headers, starts a SERVER span named by the
request method, and records the status. A malformed traceparent starts a new
trace and never fails the request.

symbols.name: ServiceNameKey
symbols.doc:
ServiceNameKey is the resource attribute a backend joins a trace to a metric
on. It is the same constant pkg/v1/observe/metrics exports, so the two signals cannot
disagree about the spelling.

symbols.name: Span
symbols.doc: Span is one live, recording span. FROZEN at five methods (ADR 0039).

symbols.name: SpanContext
symbols.doc:
SpanContext is the immutable identity of a span — what travels in a
traceparent and what a child inherits.

symbols.name: SpanContextFromContext
symbols.doc:
SpanContextFromContext returns the span context carried by ctx, or the invalid
zero value when there is none.

symbols.name: SpanData
symbols.doc:
SpanData is one FINISHED span — what a SpanSink receives and an exporter
ships. The live one is [Span].

symbols.name: SpanExporter
symbols.doc: SpanExporter ships a batch of finished spans to a backend.

symbols.name: SpanID
symbols.doc:
SpanID identifies one span: eight octets, rendered as 16 lowercase hex
digits. The all-zero value is invalid, and is also how "no parent" is spelled.

symbols.name: SpanParams
symbols.doc:
SpanParams are the facts a span is born with. The zero value is an INTERNAL
span starting now.

symbols.name: SpanSink
symbols.doc: SpanSink receives every sampled span at End. A func port, for the same reason.

symbols.name: Spans
symbols.doc:
Spans is a batch of finished spans plus the Resource and Scope that describe
all of them.

symbols.name: Status
symbols.doc: Status is a span's recorded outcome.

symbols.name: StatusCode
symbols.doc: StatusCode is a span's verdict: unset, ok or error.

symbols.name: StatusError
symbols.doc: StatusError is a failure.

symbols.name: StatusOK
symbols.doc: StatusOK is an explicit success assertion by the developer.

symbols.name: StatusUnset
symbols.doc:
StatusUnset is the default: no explicit judgement. It does NOT mean "it
worked" — a backend applies its own heuristics, and claiming OK on the
caller's behalf would suppress them.

symbols.name: String
symbols.doc: String returns a string-valued attribute.

symbols.name: TraceFlags
symbols.doc: TraceFlags is the traceparent flag byte. Only bit 0, sampled, is defined.

symbols.name: TraceID
symbols.doc:
TraceID identifies one trace: sixteen octets, rendered as 32 lowercase hex
digits. The all-zero value is invalid.

symbols.name: TraceParentHeader
symbols.doc: TraceParentHeader is the W3C header carrying the span context.

symbols.name: TraceParentLen
symbols.doc: TraceParentLen is the length of a version-00 traceparent: 55 characters.

symbols.name: TraceState
symbols.doc:
TraceState is the parsed tracestate header: an ordered vendor list, leftmost
first. Immutable.

symbols.name: TraceStateHeader
symbols.doc: TraceStateHeader is the W3C header carrying the vendor list.

symbols.name: Tracer
symbols.doc: Tracer starts spans. FROZEN at one method (ADR 0039).

symbols.name: TracerConfig
symbols.doc:
TracerConfig configures a Tracer. Every field has a resolved meaning
when left unset.

symbols.name: URLFullKey
symbols.doc: URLFullKey is the outbound URL attribute, recorded on CLIENT spans.

symbols.name: URLPathKey
symbols.doc: URLPathKey is the inbound request path attribute, in its ESCAPED form.

symbols.name: URLSchemeKey
symbols.doc: URLSchemeKey is the request scheme attribute.

symbols.name: UnknownExporter

code.public: No trace exporter is registered under that name

symbols.doc: UnknownExporter reports a name no imported package registered.

symbols.name: VersionSupported
symbols.doc: VersionSupported is the traceparent version this SDK emits: "00".
